intro: Ban Chahomm Guesthouse is a small place to stay in Betong district, Yala, on Atthawethi Road. It is a newer property that does not have many reviews yet, but the guests who have stayed agree on the same things: the rooms are spotless, the beds are comfortable and the staff look after you well. body.html: Ban Chahomm Guesthouse is a small property in Betong district, Yala province, on Atthawethi Road. It is a newer guesthouse without many reviews yet, but you can already see the direction guests are leaning — positive enough that it earned a Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice badge early on. The place feels more like a guesthouse than a hotel: simple, friendly and easygoing, a good fit for travellers coming to Betong on a modest budget who just want a clean room to sleep in.

The two things guests mention most are cleanliness and the private balconies. Every room has a balcony looking out over a garden and the mountains — some are city-view — plus a shared terrace and outdoor seating where you can come down and enjoy Betong's cool morning air. Rooms are air-conditioned and come with a flat-screen TV, fridge, kettle, minibar, private bathroom, hairdryer and toiletries, with free Wi-Fi throughout. The basics are well covered for a budget guesthouse.
"Clean room, comfortable bed, a balcony to chill on, and it's only about ten minutes' walk to the clock tower. The staff are lovely and speak both Thai and Chinese."

Service is another point in its favour. Reception staff speak Thai, English and Chinese, which helps a lot in Betong with its steady flow of Malaysian and Chinese visitors. Several guests say the owner and staff are attentive and good at recommending where to eat and what to see. The location is in town — about a 9-minute walk to the Betong Clock Tower and roughly 11 minutes to the World's Largest Mailbox, with plenty of restaurants within walking distance.

If you are driving to Betong, the guesthouse has free on-site parking, which is handy for heading out to the sights beyond town such as the Aiyerweng sea of mist, the Skywalk or the hot springs. One thing to know in advance is the deposit — the property collects a THB 500 damage deposit at check-in, paid in cash and refunded at check-out after a room inspection. This is normal for small guesthouses, so it helps to carry some cash.

Bear in mind this is a guesthouse, not a full-service hotel. There is no swimming pool, no lift like a large hotel, and the listing does not state that breakfast is included. Check-in is 13:00 and check-out is 12:00. Betong is famous for its morning dim sum, though, and the shops are not far, so most people head out for breakfast anyway. With only a handful of rooms, it fills up quickly over long Thai holiday weekends, so book ahead.

In short, Ban Chahomm Guesthouse suits travellers who come to Betong on a budget and value cleanliness and a friendly, homey feel over a full set of facilities. The real strengths are the spotless rooms, the garden/mountain-view balconies, attentive multilingual staff and free parking. Just accept that reviews are still few, so some details are thin, and there is no pool or hotel-style service. If you want a pool or full facilities, compare it with the central Betong hotels — but if you want a clean, good-value room in a walkable spot, this is a solid pick.

A tip from reading the reviews: have THB 500 in cash ready for the check-in deposit, and ask for a room whose balcony faces the garden and mountains to get the view that is this place's selling point. If you arrive by car, let the guesthouse know about parking in advance. And because it is a small property with few rooms, book early over festivals and pick a free-cancellation rate if your plans are not yet firm.

faq.q: Where is Ban Chahomm Guesthouse and what's within walking distance?
faq.a: It's at 9/1 Atthawethi Road, Betong district, Yala, in town. It's about a 9-minute walk to the Betong Clock Tower and roughly 11 minutes to the World's Largest Mailbox, with restaurants and sights such as Wat Kuan Im and the street art within walking distance — easy to explore the town on foot.

faq.q: How much does Ban Chahomm Guesthouse cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at approximately ฿850/night for a standard room, around ฿950 for a garden-view room and about ฿1,200 for a family room. Rates vary by date and holidays, so always compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is there a swimming pool or breakfast?
faq.a: There is no swimming pool, and the listing does not state that breakfast is included. Every room has a private balcony, A/C, fridge, kettle and minibar. Betong is famous for its morning dim sum and the shops are within walking distance, so most guests head out for breakfast.

faq.q: Is there a deposit, and what are the check-in times?
faq.a: The guesthouse takes a THB 500 damage deposit at check-in, paid in cash and refunded at check-out after a room inspection. Check-in is 13:00 and check-out is 12:00 — it helps to have some cash on hand.

faq.q: Who is Ban Chahomm Guesthouse best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers on a budget who want a clean room and a friendly, homey feel. Highlights are the garden/mountain-view balconies, staff who speak Thai, English and Chinese, and free parking. If you want a pool or full hotel-style service, also compare the central Betong hotels.
